concept.title: Sharp Constant for Odd Franel Cube Sums
concept.concept_description:
The proved estimate franel(2m+1)*(3m+1) <= 8^(2m+1) is off by a factor of about 2.7 from the true asymptotics franel(n) ~ 2*sqrt(3)*8^n/(3*pi*n). Sharpening it would make the inversion threshold provable uniformly in parity with no finite case check.

For all n >= 1, 2*franel(n)*n <= 8^n, with the constant 2 asymptotically optimal up to sqrt(3)/pi.

Induction on n using the Franel recurrence (n+1)^2 F(n+1) = (7n^2+7n+2) F(n) + 8 n^2 F(n-1), verified numerically for n <= 40 by exact evaluation.

One clean estimate replaces both parity cases and the small-bitlen checks in the threshold theorem.

The crude max-times-total bound is essentially the only elementary route, and thresholds must stay case-split.

concept.title: Base Threshold for Octave-Equivalence Faithfulness
concept.concept_description:
Pitch-class reduction modulo twelve is injective on decimal digits, so octave equivalence is vacuous there, but it fails from base thirteen on. We conjecture a sharp threshold with quantitative divergence of the interval-class and interval histograms.

Pitch-class reduction is injective on base-b digits iff b <= 12; for b >= 13 there are melodies whose interval-class and interval histograms differ in total variation by at least (b - 12)/b.

Generalize pitchClass_inj_of_lt to arbitrary bases, then construct explicit melodies in base b >= 13 whose folded histogram collapses two distinct interval values.

Mod-12 analyses of digit melodies are provably content-free precisely in the bases used by decimal studies.

Octave folding carries information even below base thirteen, which would change how interval classes should be reported.
concept.mathematical_framing:
Pitch-class reduction modulo twelve is injective on decimal digits, so octave equivalence is vacuous there, but it fails from base thirteen on. We conjecture a sharp threshold with quantitative divergence of the interval-class and interval histograms.

Generalize pitchClass_inj_of_lt to arbitrary bases, then construct explicit melodies in base b >= 13 whose folded histogram collapses two distinct interval values.

concept.lean_guess: Injectivity is Nat.mod_eq_of_lt; failure uses the pair (0, 12); the total-variation bound counts the digit pairs whose distance exceeds eleven.

concept.title: A closed form for `∑_{k ≤ a} S(n,k)` for every fixed `a ≥ 4`.
concept.concept_description:
A closed form for `∑_{k ≤ a} S(n,k)` for every fixed `a ≥ 4`.  The cases `a = 2` and
   `a = 3` are now proved here (`card_orbits_binary`, `card_orbits_ternary`), and the
   pattern of the two proofs — expand the truncated row, apply `stirling2_succ_succ` to each
   term, and close with `omega` — suggests that for each fixed `a` the orbit count satisfies
   the linear recurrence with characteristic roots `1, 2, …, a`; the conjecture is that this
   holds uniformly in `a` and matches `∑_{j ≤ a} (-1)^{a-j} j^n / (j! (a-j)!)`.

concept.title: Tropical Crystallization Threshold
concept.concept_description:
The Maslov gap and the top-1 margin bound each other two-sidedly. Conjecture that for random score vectors the gap concentrates, producing a sharp threshold at margin ~ log n separating tropical (max-like) from diffuse (soft) layers.

For x with i.i.d. sub-Gaussian coordinates and top-1 margin m, the Maslov gap concentrates around log(1 + (n-1) E e^{-m}) with fluctuations O(1/sqrt n), so the tropical/diffuse boundary is a sharp threshold in m at log n.

Prove concentration for the Gaussian case in Lean using the two-sided bounds maslovGap_le_of_margin and margin_le_of_maslovGap, then check numerically against measured per-layer gap medians.

Crystallization is a property of the margin distribution, not of the trained weights, and can be predicted before training.

The tail's large Maslov gap reflects weight structure and must be explained by the learned attention geometry.
